Definition: Zocheleth, a boundary stone in. Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Zoheleth is the stone by En-rogel, near Jerusalem, where Adonijah held his feast and sacrificed sheep and oxen while claiming the throne for himself. The stone's name means 'serpent,' and it is the same stone the place records call the Serpent's Stone. Adonijah's feast at that stone ended in nothing — Solomon was anointed king while the guests were still eating.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the stone is a warning carved into the landscape: a feast thrown to steal a throne cannot stand against the king God has chosen.
